plan.analysis: 0.9407938 has resisted ~30 structurally different escapes; only fine-grid re-optimisation (+6e-6 once), clip/window polish and prune-unzero ever paid, all ~1e-6. I bet this is a near-optimal local max: further gains, if any, need (a) a combination of the historically productive ingredients (fine repeat grid + concentrated free set + zoned shake), (b) a test that the support pattern is rigid under large-scale rearrangements (never tried; all previous support moves were 1-3 cells or block translations), and (c) an actual headroom measurement by relaxing h>=0 to the convex cone {L>=0, rfft(L)>=0} in L-space, which bounds what any h-based search could ever reach.

experiments.hypothesis: p0306's +6e-6 came from re-optimising the same function at N=84992, but full-vector L-BFGS dilutes that gradient over 85k coordinates and every later fine-grid run was full-vector. Restricting the free set at the fine grid to the 1-cell neighbourhoods of the existing spikes concentrates all curvature exactly where the grid-limited taper lives, and the zoned prune/unzero shake (which only pays on the 65.8%-zero 42496 representation, never the all-positive one) supplies the missing support change.
experiments.change: In construct, after loading/rescaling start, add a loop that runs until deadline-3.0: (1) hf = np.repeat(best, 2) (exact, R preserved); (2) free = union over i with hf[i]>0 of {i-1,i,i+1} (clip to range) — pass this as free= to _exact_lbfgs(hf,1200,2400,deadline); (3) then _exact_lbfgs(hf,800,1600,deadline) full and _window_polish(hf,deadline); if R strictly improves keep the 84992 array as best and continue; (4) otherwise coarsen best to 42496 by block-mean, zero all cells < 1e-4*max, set 200 random zero cells to 1e-3*mean, run _exact_lbfgs at 42496, np.repeat back to 84992, run _exact_lbfgs at 84992, keep on strict gain. Keep p0394's existing stages after this loop but with the deadline guards intact.
experiments.prediction: Either a reproducible small gain (+1e-6..+3e-6) coming from step 2/3 while step 4 accepts nothing, or the score stays exactly 0.9407938 with every phase reporting identical R — the latter would confirm the fine-grid freedom is exhausted even with a concentrated free set.

experiments.hypothesis: All support-level moves so far were single-cell toggles, 1-3 cell shifts, or block translations of length <=34 (F380, F398, F404); these preserve only very local geometry. A large-scale rearrangement (mirroring a 64-2048 cell block in place, or exchanging two distant equal-length blocks) keeps each block's internal difference multiset while globally reshuffling cross-differences, a coordinated move on the sum-set that no experiment has made, and the exact R + local-window repolish makes each trial cheap.
experiments.change: Insert a new stage in construct right after the start is loaded and rescaled, before the existing clip/beta ladders: for up to 40 trials while time < deadline-3.0: pick W uniformly from {64,128,256,512,1024,2048} and a uniformly random a inside [first_nonzero, last_nonzero-W]; with equal probability do either (i) h'=best.copy(); h'[a:a+W]=best[a:a+W][::-1], or (ii) pick b with |a-b|>4W and swap the two length-W blocks; then polish with the base's _exact_lbfgs restricted to free=np.arange(max(0,a-32), min(n,a+W+32)) (plus the b window for case ii), followed by a full _exact_lbfgs and one _window_polish; accept only on strict R gain (revert otherwise). Then run p0329's unchanged pipeline on the best.
experiments.prediction: Zero accepts: R returns exactly 0.9407938, showing the sum-set pattern is rigid under block-level rearrangement as well as under local shifts, which rules out the 'wrong discrete pattern' hypothesis at every scale.

experiments.hypothesis: Every failure so far optimises over h with the h>=0 and 'L is a square' structure baked in, so nobody knows whether 0.9408 is limited by that structure or by the objective itself. Since L=h*h is exactly equivalent to rfft(L)>=0 with L>=0, the set C={L>=0, rfft(L)>=0} is a convex cone containing every achievable L; maximising the same R(L) over C gives a rigorous numerical upper-bound estimate on headroom and, if the relaxed optimum is far above, tells us the binding constraint is the nonneg square root rather than the flat-top profile.
experiments.change: Add a diagnostic stage at the very start of construct, before any polishing: downsample best to Nc=192 by block-mean and rescale. Work with L on M=384 points (knot grid, L[0]=L[-1]=0). Implement proj(L) = 30 alternating/Dykstra steps of L<-np.clip(L,0,None) and L<-np.fft.irfft(np.clip(np.fft.rfft(L),0,None), M). Run projected gradient ascent (Barzilai-Borwein step, ~1500 iterations, gradient of -log Q + 2 log mass + log-sum-exp(max L) with eps annealed 1e-2 -> 1e-6, where Q and mass are computed from L with the exact knot formula) and print 'R_relax=%.6f vs coarse incumbent=%.6f'. Then attempt recovery: h_rec = np.fft.irfft(np.sqrt(np.clip(np.fft.rfft(Lb),0,None)),M) clipped >=0, polish at Nc with _exact_lbfgs, upsample by np.repeat to best.size and run the base pipeline; keep only on strict R gain.
experiments.prediction: R_relax lands clearly above the coarse incumbent (0.95-0.99), proving large headroom exists in the convex relaxation yet the recovered h never beats 0.9407938 — i.e. the gap is caused by the nonneg-square-root structure, not by the flat-top target, and further h-space polishing of this basin is futile.

plan.analysis: The 0.940794 point has now survived 34+ structurally different attacks (F383, F410, F414, F415, F418), and the trapezoid algebra says a real gain needs the effective taper shortened by ~20% relative — far beyond the 1e-6 noise the local levers produce. So I bet one experiment on a still-untried surrogate (Chebyshev equalisation of the near-max band, exploiting R = num/(s^2·maxL)), and two on genuinely different basins: the smooth low-N branch (p0416, the only family that improved last generation) climbed by resolution continuation, and a free-form coarse (N=2656) multistart with a ladder back up, which has never been run without a restricted profile family.

experiments.hypothesis: R = num/(s^2·maxL), so flattening the top band (lowering the high knots and lifting the floor) raises R even at fixed num; existing surrogates either shave only knots above c (clip, F325/F410) or reward the band (F374), but none minimise the Chebyshev spread of the whole band at a free running level, which is the direct definition of the residual flat-top loss.
experiments.change: Add `_band_obj_grad(h, lo, hi)`: compute num, dq, Lf = _num_and_dq(h); m = Lf.max(); idx = (Lf >= lo*m) & (Lf <= hi*m); c = mean(Lf[idx]); r = (Lf - c) * idx; obj = 0.5*np.sum(r*r); gLf = r (r[i]=0 outside idx); gLf[0]=gLf[-1]=0; grad = _backprop(gLf, h); return obj, grad. Add `run_band(h0, lo, hi, maxiter, maxfun, deadline)` mirroring run_clip (L-BFGS-B, bounds (0,None), ftol 1e-17, gtol 1e-13, timeout callback). In construct, right after the start is loaded and rescaled and before Stage A, insert a loop `for _ in range(6)` that breaks if time > deadline-2.0: for (lo,hi) in [(0.9,1.0),(0.6,1.0),(0.3,1.0),(0.1,1.0)]: cand = run_band(best, lo, hi, 400, 800, deadline); cand = _exact_lbfgs(cand, 400, 800, deadline); if R_of(cand) > bestR+1e-15 accept and print. Keep all of p0394 after that unchanged.
experiments.prediction: Either one band level gives a real gain of 1e-5..1e-6 (then the plateau's loss is band ripple, not taper), or every level returns exactly 0.940794 — which would say the band is already Chebyshev-optimal and confirms the loss is the taper geometry, killing all near-max surrogates at once.

experiments.hypothesis: p0416's N=174 smooth shape is the only family that improved last generation (F419), and it lives in a different basin than the jagged incumbent. Repeated doubling with re-optimisation at every level (instead of one final polish) lets the shape adapt phase-by-phase; trying both linear-interp and zero-order-hold at each level avoids locking into the wrong sub-cell phase (the failure mode of F406/F330).
experiments.change: In p0416's construct, replace the body after loading `start` with a resolution ladder: h = rescaled start (N0 ≈ 174); loop while h.size < 100000 and time < deadline-2.5: build two candidates ha = np.interp(linspace(0,n-1,2n), arange(n), h) and hb = np.repeat(h,2); polish each with the file's exact-LBFGS (300 iters, 600 funs) on log-active coordinates; take whichever has higher R_of (tie -> linear); record (size, R). Then take the best-R rung, run full exact L-BFGS (1500/3000) plus the peak-window polish to the deadline, accepting only strict gains over bestR; print each rung's R. Return best.

plan.analysis: The 0.940794 basin has now absorbed ~50 structurally different escapes (F383), and the one genuine +1e-6 came from a top-K max proxy (F446) whose K ladder only reached 20, whereas F289's much wider K (4000..1) paid +1.1e-5 on a weaker basin — so the near-max band's tail has not been tried here. experiments.prediction: The projection is infeasible (no h gives a clean 0/1 L), so the re-solve lands at or below 0.940794; a gain >5e-6 would mean the taper mass is genuinely shaveable.

experiments.hypothesis: The taper is a *smooth* slope; TV(L)=sum|L_{j+1}-L_j| penalises that slope only once (2*max for a perfect cliff) while raising the plateau floor, so a decreasing-lambda TV continuation drives the shape toward cliffs and out of the smooth-taper local optimum — a regulariser not yet tried (prior ones penalised the band by value, not by slope).

experiments.prediction: Either a gain of 1e-5-5e-5 (TV continuation reaches a crisper plateau/taper trade) or exactly 0.940794, showing the incumbent's taper is already TV-minimal for its plateau length.

info.open_why: p0435 is the shared base of the current best lineage; F383 is the most-cited finding explaining the 0.940794 plateau; F446/F427/F426/F295 cover the prune-and-repolish and upsample levers that worked on other basins, to judge whether they can transfer here.

plan.analysis: The 0.940794 basin has absorbed ~60 structurally different escapes (F383), and the last real gain there was +1e-6. Decomposing R = ∫L²/∫L with max L = 1 shows the whole 5.9% deficit is L-mass below 1: plateau ripple plus the (right-long, per F391) taper. Smoothing/targeting/max-proxy surrogates all failed because they perturb values globally; what remains untested are (a) polishing the taper-generating support ends as the free set (window polish has historically paid exactly on this basin only because full L-BFGS is ill-conditioned), (b) the axis-warp direction, orthogonal to every height-space move, and (c) changing spike *width* at fixed positions, which F349/F352 never did (they conserved mass across both halves, leaving width unchanged).

experiments.hypothesis: The residual loss is L-mass in the taper, and the heights generating it (cells at the two support ends) have never been the free set: every window polish (F316, F375, F376, F442) freed the argmax/flat-top region instead. Because full-vector L-BFGS at 42k is ill-conditioned, a tight-tolerance polish confined to the taper-generating ends can still move R, as F316 did by +4e-6 with a different free set.
experiments.change: Keep p0454's code. Add _taper_free(h): compute Lf=_knots(h), mx=Lf.max(); k_lo=smallest k with Lf[k]>=0.999*mx, k_hi=largest; let n=h.size, support_lo=first index with h>1e-13*h.max(), support_hi=last; free = indices in [support_lo, support_lo + max(8,int(0.10*neff))] plus [support_hi - max(8,int(0.25*neff)), support_hi], neff=support_hi-support_lo+1, also include the 8 cells adjacent to every knot index near k_lo and k_hi (i.e. cells |k_lo-1-i| small, mirrored). Call _exact_lbfgs(h, 3000, 6000, deadline, free=free) with ftol 1e-22/gtol 1e-18 (add these as parameters if the current call hardcodes 1e-20/1e-16), then a _full_polish, accept only if R_of improves on 0.940794. Loop this taper-polish/full-polish alternation until deadline-1.0, keeping the best.
experiments.prediction: Either +1e-6..+5e-6 (taper window is a genuine under-converged direction) or exactly 0.940794 returned unchanged, which would show the taper is at its constrained optimum and the ends are already stationary.

experiments.hypothesis: Every move so far is a perturbation of the heights; the axis warp (a monotone reparametrization of cell edges, which changes the shape without changing the heights) is an orthogonal direction that only F397 touched, and only as a 2-parameter plateau-boundary shift. A smooth 8-parameter warp direction is not in the span of any height gradient at the optimum, so if the incumbent is suboptimal along it, exact-R improves.
experiments.change: Add _warp(h, y): y = 9 increasing breakpoints in [0,1], cell edges in old coordinates x_j = n*y(j/n) (n=h.size), new height = mass-conserving cell average of h over [x_j, x_{j+1}], i.e. via cumulative sum of h and np.interp on the cumsum (clip >=0, then _rescale_maxL). Parametrize y_i = clip((i/8) + 0.03*tanh(a_i)) with the 8 free a_i, forced monotone by sorting. Optimize a on exact R_of with Nelder-Mead (maxiter 300, xatol 1e-3) evaluated on a 4000-cell block-averaged copy of h for speed; take the best a, build the full-resolution warped h, run _full_polish plus one _window_polish, accept only if R exceeds 0.940794. With leftover time repeat with the found warp as the new base (second warp round) and then run the existing polish loop.
experiments.prediction: Exactly 0.940794 (+0.000000) is the most likely outcome (the shape is flat along warps too); a gain of 1e-6..2e-5 would mean the true limiting constraint is positional, not per-cell mass, and should be followed by a warp ladders in later generations.

Placing each cell's mass in a single 1/4-width sub-cell at 4x resolution is the first real narrowing test, and it hands the optimizer 4x finer control of spike positions/widths.

plan.analysis: The 0.940794 point is now confirmed by ~70 generations of failed escapes: local polish, upsampling (linear/Gaussian/ZOH/repeat), smooth-max and top-K surrogates, prune/regrow, axis warps (8-param and per-edge), signed/spectral inits, superpositions, coarse multistarts, SA, multigrid. It is a machine-precision local max of the discrete problem (F462), so only a *structurally different construction* or a *new discrete degree of freedom* can help. I therefore spend one bet on the correct real spectral square root (previous signed attempts used sqrt(max(g,0)), destroying the sign structure), one on a combinatorial search over the phase at scale (a lever never searched systematically), and one on a sensitivity-based (not height-based) compression/regrowth, the only pruning lever not yet tried.

plan.analysis: Every structural escape, phase/spectral restart, upsampling, pruning, and oracle move has returned exactly 0.940794, so the incumbent is very likely a genuine KKT point of the exact objective. I bet at most on (i) yielding a tiny gain; (ii) and (iii) are cheap, informative gambles with real (if modest) upside.

experiments.hypothesis: All polish stages optimise u=log(h); with heights spanning ~2 orders of magnitude the L-BFGS metric is badly scaled and zero-bound cells are frozen forever. plan.analysis: The 0.940794 basin has survived ~40 generations and every structural lever: resolution doubling, coarse restarts, prunes, warps, spectral square roots, algebraic combs, multistart families. The one diagnostic signal still unexplained is that the reported argmax of f*f moves between runs (0.209/0.244/0.293/0.437/0.746/0.837 of support) with 19.6% of knots within 0.1% of max — the top is orders-flatter than the pinning gradient, so the point is a near-degenerate plateau. I bet on three angles not yet tried: continuation in the *exponent* of the max term (a new continuation axis), x-block coordinate descent (is the plateau localised in support?), and a Metropolis-accepting random walk on the exact R (all previous kicks were accept-only-improvements, so they could never drift along the plateau).

experiments.hypothesis: Every continuation tried so far (penalty mu, LSE eps, top-K, resolution, TV, smoothing) is a deformation of the *heights*; the max-term exponent has never been continued. plan.analysis: The incumbent 0.9407944 is saturated against ~100 structurally different levers; every deformation of the heights, every continuation, every upsample, every discrete repair returns the identical value, and the three other basins found (0.9396, 0.9402, 0.9403) are strictly worse. Note the reported f*f argmax position varies wildly (0.209 to 0.97) while R is identical — the top ~20% of knots are tied to <0.1%, so the max is degenerate and height-space descent is pinned by an arbitrary tie-break. Remaining upside can only come from a different state space, a genuinely un-tried shape family, or second-order information. I bet on: optimizing the autocorrelation L directly in the cone {L>=0, rfft(L)>=0}; an explicit geometric-rectangle multi-scale family with analytic plateau mechanism; and a Lanczos spectrum probe of the incumbent with subspace Newton ascent if any positive curvature exists.

experiments.hypothesis: R depends only on the knot sequence L (num, sum, max), and L is any vector in the convex cone C = {L >= 0, rfft(L) >= 0}. Optimizing R directly over C at moderate M with exact cone projections explores a state space that no height-space search touches, and any L that improves R_coarse can be converted back to h = irfft(sqrt(rfft(L))) exactly (verified by the real check).
experiments.change: Add a new stage after the K-ladder/polish (keep existing code intact; use remaining budget). (2) Analytic gradient of -log cR w.r.t. Lc (num is quadratic: dnum_j = (2L_{j-1}+L_j)/3-ish same as _num_and_dq; den = (trapz(Lc)) * max(Lc)). (3) Projected steepest/BFGS ascent with projection = 25 alternating clips: time-domain clip at 0, then irfft(max(rfft(.),0)), then time clip again. (4) Run from Lc and from 12 log-multiplicative perturbations of Lc (sigma 0.05-0.3). (5) For every candidate with cR above the incumbent's cR, pad Lc to length 2M-1, recover hc = irfft(sqrt(max(rfft(pad(Lc)),0))) (length M), resample hc to 42496 by cumulative-mass interpolation, run _exact_lbfgs + _window_polish, accept only if exact R_of > bestR. info.open_why: Need to see the current best program's actual code and the key findings about why the 0.940794 plateau resists all perturbations, to pick experiments that target a genuinely untested axis.

plan.analysis: The 0.940794 point is saturated against ~90 structurally different levers (F383/F472/F484/F485), so the realistic bet is not a new basin but a sharper attack on the one thing that costs R: the shoulders, where loss ∝ Σ L(M−L) peaks at L≈M/2. Existing free-set experiments freed support-end cells (F456) or contiguous halves/peak windows (F480, F316), never the cells generating the mid-band L knots; target-fitting experiments thresholded the incumbent (F451) or used raised-cosine/LP targets (F391/F463) but never scanned a *wider* flat top. Also unexploited: the end-knot jump costs (1/3)L_0², which is minimised iff L_0=max, i.e. h_0²=max — the incumbent pays a wide shoulder instead. Three bets, one on each.

experiments.hypothesis: The relative loss is Σ_j L_j(M-L_j)/(M ΣL_j), maximised for knots at L≈M/2, so the heights that *generate the shoulder band* are the productive free variables; making them the L-BFGS free set (rather than the peak window or the support ends) lets exact descent act where the loss lives.
experiments.change: After the usual K-ladder and first full polish, add a stage that loops until deadline-2 s: (1) compute Lf=_knots(best) and M=Lf.max(); select band = {j : 0.3M <= Lf[j] <= 0.7M}; (2) using the analytic backprop gradient of -log R at best, compute per-cell sensitivity s_i = h_i * sum_{j in band} |dLf_j/dh_i| (dLf_j/dh_i = 2*h_{j-i} for valid indices), take the top 3000 cells as `free`; (3) run _exact_lbfgs(best, 2000, 4000, deadline, free=free) then _full_polish; keep only if R_of improves; (4) if no improvement, widen the band to [0.1,0.9]M and repeat once with 5000 cells. Print band size, cell count and R after each round. Spend the remaining budget alternating band-polish and full polish.
experiments.prediction: Exact R stays 0.9407944 (+0.0000000 or at most +1e-6); the shoulder knots are already at their constrained optimum, which would confirm that the taper loss is not a free-set artifact.

experiments.hypothesis: The two end knots contribute (1/3)L_0^2 and (1/3)L_{2N-2}^2 of avoidable loss; this vanishes iff L_0=L_{2N-2}=max L, i.e. h_0=h_{N-1}=sqrt(max L), with L_1=2h_0h_1>=max forcing h_1>=h_0/2. The incumbent instead starts low and pays a wide shoulder, so a spike-ended initialisation should reach a different stationary point with a wider flat top.
experiments.change: Add a stage before the K-ladder: (1) M = max(_knots(best)); (2) build a seed by copying best, then set h[0]=h[n-1]=sqrt(M), h[1]=h[n-2]=(M-h[0]^2)/(2*h[0]) clipped to >=0 (fall back to sqrt(M)/2 if nonpositive), and h[2],h[n-3] from the recursion sum_{i=0..k} h_i h_{k-i} = M solved for h_k, for k=2,3; (3) crossfade this seed into best over the outer 5% of the support with a cosine weight so the interior is untouched; (4) _exact_lbfgs (ftol 1e-24, maxiter 3000) then _window_polish, accept only on exact-R gain; (5) repeat with the spike amplitude scaled by 0.8 and 1.2. Print max L, L_0/maxL and R for each attempt, then continue with the base pipeline on whichever is best.
experiments.prediction: The spike-ended seed polishes back to R <= 0.9407944; its L_0/maxL lands near 1 with a visibly narrower shoulder but no gain, showing the end-jump term is not the binding constraint.

Since R = 1 - ∫L(M-L)/(M·mass²), the only remaining freedom is the taper, and the taper has resisted every surrogate. plan.analysis: The 0.940794 point is saturated against ~90 structurally different moves (F383/F472/F484/F495/F500): local polishes, upsampling, warps, spectral/signed constructions, arcsinse seeds, symmetric subspace, exact L→h inversion all return exactly 0.940794. The blame is repeatedly placed on two things: (i) the max-term pins a single argmax knot so the gradient cannot move the near-max band, and (ii) any reparametrization that keeps h nonneg lands in the same basin. So I bet on three genuinely different *levers on the optimization geometry* rather than new shapes: a max-free (quotient) gradient, an over-parametrized product factorization, and resolution added only where the loss lives (the taper).

experiments.hypothesis: The objective's log(max L) term pins one argmax knot (F451/F409/F414), so L-BFGS cannot move the 19.6% near-max band. If instead the objective is the scale-quotient -log(num)+2log(s) evaluated on h renormalized to max(L)=1 *inside* f (stop-gradient through the rescale), the gradient is a pure shape derivative spread over ALL knots and the argmax term disappears; this is a different gradient field from every LSE/top-K/penalty surrogate tried.
experiments.change: Add a stage after the first full polish (keep all existing code): implement `_quot_fun_grad(h)`: (1) h<0->0; if sum<=0 fail; (2) r = 1/sqrt(max(_knots(h))), hr = h*r; (3) num,dq,Lf=_num_and_dq(hr); s=hr.sum(); (4) val=-log(num)+2log(s), gLf=-dq/num, gLf += 1/s (uniform, from the sum term is 2/s d s/d hr = 2/s → use gLf += 2.0/s on all entries? no: implement as val=-log(num)+2log(s) with grad = _backprop(-dq/num, hr) + 2.0/s; ) (5) return val, grad*hr (log-param chain rule, hr not h). Then `_exact_lbfgs` variant that uses `_quot_fun_grad` instead of `_norm_eq_fun_grad` (free = all positive cells), maxiter 3000, plus window polish; accept only on exact R_of gain; then run the base's alternating full/window loop to deadline. experiments.prediction: The quotient stage converges to exactly 0.940794 (same basin) but with the argmax knot possibly shifted; no gain. If it prints a strictly higher R, the argmax-pinning explanation was right and the win survives the exact-R check.

I bet the remaining upside is not in local h-space descent. Two experiments leave h-space: optimize R over the convex cone of valid knot sequences L (a strict relaxation of {h*h : h>=0}, so it exposes headroom and yields a principled target), and a derivative-free global search at coarse N with laddering. The third refines the incumbent through exact L-space deconvolution rather than height interpolation, which avoids the kinks every upsample attempt introduced.

experiments.hypothesis: R depends only on L=h*h, and the set of valid L is the convex cone C={L>=0, rfft(L)>=0}, which strictly contains autoconvolutions of nonneg h. Ascending R inside C finds the relaxed optimum; if R_cone >> 0.940794 but the incumbent is already the best nonneg realization, we learn the loss is the h>=0 constraint, and the cone-optimal L* gives a principled target to least-squares fit with h.
experiments.change: Add after the base's first full polish: (1) `_cone_ascent(g, deadline)`: g = interior knot vector of the incumbent, length m=2N-1; loop while time remains: evaluate exact R(g) with its analytic gradient (dq from _num_and_dq; den = (trapz over the symmetric embedding of g)^2 * max(g)); take gradient step, clip g>=0, then project onto the cone by F=rfft(symmetric_embed(g)), F=maximum(F,0), g=irfft(F) re-symmetrised and re-clipped >=0; backtrack the step until R(g) improves; track best g and print R_cone. (2) Take best g as target L* (rescaled to max 1) and run 3 rounds of residual fitting: minimise 0.5*sum((conv(h,h)-L*)^2) over h>0 in log-parametrisation with analytic gradient 2*correlate(residual,h) (L-BFGS-B, maxiter 400), each round followed by one full exact polish, keeping only exact-R improvements. Then fall back into the base's alternating full/window polish loop until deadline.
experiments.prediction: R_cone rises clearly above 0.940794 (real relaxation headroom), but the fitted nonneg h never exceeds 0.940794; any h with R>0.940794 after the fit is a new best and proves the incumbent was h-limited.

experiments.hypothesis: All global searches so far were smooth-family multistarts, SA with multiplicative proposals at N=512 (F445), or coarse block discovery (F403) and were budget-starved. A population method with self-adapting covariance (differential evolution) over a log-parametrised coarse step array, run to convergence at N=96 and then laddered up, searches a genuinely wider set of coarse profiles within seconds and could reveal a second basin above 0.940794.
experiments.change: Keep the base code; after its first full polish, if >8 s remain: run scipy.optimize.differential_evolution on exact R of a length-96 array (parameters = log heights, bounds [-12,2], init='sobol', popsize=20, maxiter=40, tol=0, polish=True, seed in {1,2,3}) with a callback raising TimeoutError past a 6 s sub-deadline; take the 3 best distinct candidates (exact R at N=96). For each, ladder: mass-conserving linear upsample x2 -> _exact_lbfgs(400 iters) -> _window_polish, repeating to N=42496, adopting only exact-R improvements over bestR (print each rung). Then run the base's alternating full/window polish to the deadline.
experiments.prediction: DE converges to coarse profiles with R≈0.90-0.94; after laddering every candidate lands at or below 0.940794 and the start is returned. A strictly better laddered result would prove a second basin exists.

experiments.hypothesis: Every upsampling attempt interpolated heights, injecting kinks; but R depends only on the knot sequence L, so the right refinement is to upsample L and deconvolve. At moderate resolution the exact recursion h_0=sqrt(L_0), h_k=(L_k - sum_{i=1}^{k-1} h_i h_{k-i})/(2h_0) is affordable, so we can (a) test whether the incumbent's L is essentially a nonneg autoconvolution, (b) ascend R on L inside the cone cheaply (thousands of iterations at M=2048), and (c) recover a nonneg h exactly and ladder it with polish.
experiments.change: After the base's first full polish: block-downsample the incumbent's knot vector L (length 2N-1) to M=2048 knots (rescaled), run the O(M^2) recursion to recover h of length 1024, clip negatives to 0, print R_of(h) vs start R. Then run 5000 projected gradient ascent steps on the 2048-vector L within the cone (same projection and exact-R backtracking as described), and deconvolve the best L again. Ladder the recovered h to N=42496 by mass-conserving 2x upsample + _exact_lbfgs(400) + _window_polish at each rung, adopting only exact-R improvements; finish with the base's polish loop to the deadline.
experiments.prediction: The recursion is stable (L is nearly a nonneg autoconvolution) and R after recovery is ≈0.9407-0.9408; cone ascent adds at most a few 1e-4 in the relaxation, and the laddered h lands at 0.940794. A gain would mean the incumbent's grid representation, not its shape, is the limit.

info.open_why: p0383 is the common ancestor of the whole stuck 0.940794 subtree; F495/F451/F383 are the key findings on why the basin is frozen, and p0503/F503 show the most recent structural attempts (flat-autoconvolution family, taper-band splitting) so I can pick a genuinely different lever.

plan.analysis: Roughly 50 generations have been pinned at 0.940794, with dozens of structurally distinct escapes (spectral, cone, warps, multistart, pruning, upsampling) all returning that point, so the basin looks near-globally optimal at N=42496. Two levers are genuinely untested. (a) Zero-padding the heights is exactly R-neutral, so it hands the optimiser free cells to finish the taper if the incumbent is truncated at its support ends — zero risk, real upside. (b) The objective has only ever been optimised through a one-argmax penalty, never through a true KKT equality-constrained solve, so residual loss could be penalty slack. (c) The grid may still be resolution-limited. I bet on padding, then constrained solve, then 200k grid.

experiments.hypothesis: R depends only on the height values, so appending K zeros to each end gives bit-identical R but new degrees of freedom. If the incumbent is truncated (its end heights are not negligible) the taper of f*f is cut off at both boundaries and letting the ends decay over extra cells reduces the intermediate-knot mass, raising R; if its ends are already ~0 this is a no-op.
experiments.change: Keep all of p0509, but insert a new stage right after Stage 1b (before Stage 2's while loop). For K in (2048, 8192): build h_pad = concatenate(zeros(K), best, zeros(K)), then seed the new leading cells with best[0]*exp(-(K-j)/tau) for j=0..K-1 and the trailing cells with best[-1]*exp(-j/tau), tau = max(8.0, K/50.0), then _rescale_maxL. Verify R_of(h_pad) is within 1e-12 of bestR (padding itself is R-neutral; the seeded tail may make it lower, that is fine). Then run _full_polish(h_pad, deadline_slice, iters=400) with a deadline slice of 8 s, plus _window_polish on the result; if R_of beats bestR by >1e-12, adopt h_pad as best (N grows) and re-enter the base's alternating full/window loop at the new N until the deadline. Print the end heights of the incumbent and R after each K, and the final N.
experiments.prediction: If the incumbent is truncation-limited, R rises by >=1e-6 (possibly much more) and the printed end heights of the start are >1e-3 of max. If the printed end heights are <1e-6 of max, R stays exactly 0.940794 and the support-truncation explanation is refuted.

experiments.hypothesis: Every optimiser here uses a smooth surrogate of max(L) (log term, top-K mean, LSE or a stop-gradient rescale), so the reported point is a stationary point of a penalised objective, not of the true constrained problem. Solving maximise num(h) subject to sum(h)=1 and L_{k*}(h)=1 exactly (k* = current argmax knot fixed, so it is smooth) with an SQP method will land on a genuinely different point; if that point has higher R, the penalty formulation was leaving slack and the incumbent is not the constrained optimum.
experiments.change: Add a stage after Stage 1b: (1) compute Lf=_knots(best), k* = argmax(Lf)-1 on the raw convolution index, free set = the M=3000 cells with largest |h*grad| of the exact -log R gradient. (2) Define u=log h on the free set, and run scipy.optimize.minimize(f, u0, jac=True, method='SLSQP', bounds=[(-30,10)]*M, constraints=[{'type':'eq','fun':sum(h)-1,'jac':h}, {'type':'eq','fun':L_{k*}(h)-1,'jac':backprop(e_{k*},h)*h}], options={'maxiter':80,'ftol':1e-14}) where f = -num(h) with grad = -backprop(dq,h)*h. (3) Recompute k*, rerun if it changed. (4) Accept only if R_of improves; then continue the base's alternating full/window polish to the deadline. Print k*, R after the SQP solve, and the resulting max/mean and peak position.
experiments.prediction: The SQP solve changes the shape visibly (peak position or max/mean shifts) and yields R within ±3e-6 of 0.940794; a strictly higher R (>1e-6 gain surviving the exact-R check) refutes the claim that the penalty formulation already sits at the constrained optimum.

experiments.hypothesis: The score can only increase with the number of steps if the 42496 grid is resolution-limiting the plateau/taper corner; 84992 was tested only by starting from the upsampled incumbent, never by spending the whole budget polishing a fresh 200000-cell representation. If the true optimum has a sharper corner than 1/42496 of the support allows, a 200k polish finds it.
experiments.change: Keep p0509's first two stages to get best at N=42496, then replace Stage 2 with: (1) build h4 = piecewise-linear interpolation of best's heights onto 200000 cells (np.interp over the cumulative cell index), rescale max(L)=1; (2) run _window_polish(h4, deadline) then alternate _full_polish(h4, iters=400) and _window_polish(h4) on the 200000-cell array until the deadline, keeping only exact-R improvements and always comparing against bestR from the 42496 array; (3) if by the deadline nothing beat bestR, downsample h4 by block-averaging back to 42496, polish once, and return whichever of the two has higher R. Print R at each phase and N of the returned array.
experiments.prediction: Either R exceeds 0.940794 by <=2e-6 (grid not resolution-limited at 42k) or by >1e-5, which would show the 42496 discretisation was the binding constraint and that resolution is the remaining lever.

info.open_why: Need to see the exact incumbent algorithm, the key findings on why the 0.940794 basin is frozen (F495/F451/F383), and the most recent failed wide-loop variants (F510/F500) to pick genuinely new directions.

plan.analysis: The 0.9407944 point has survived ~80 generations and 500 findings: every local surrogate (LSE, top-K, quotient, SQP), every global family (spectral, LP, combs, warps, sub-cell splits), and every grid refinement/upsampling has returned the same value, and p0514 at N=84992 gives the same R, so the deficit (~0.059) looks like a property of the continuous shape, not the grid. Two things were never finished properly: a curvature/saddle probe (F487 ran out of budget) and the classical geometric t^{-1/2} block construction whose tapers cancel. I bet mostly on those two, plus one brute-force randomised sweep of the taper band, the only place the loss lives.

experiments.hypothesis: Linear surrogates are all pinned by the argmax knot, but if the polished point is a saddle of the exact -log R objective on the active coordinates (the plateau is degenerate, 19.6% of knots within 0.1% of max), there is a negative-curvature direction L-BFGS cannot take because it is not a descent direction. F487 tried this and died on budget; done on ~20000 log-active cells with 25 Lanczos iterations it costs only ~25 extra gradient calls.
experiments.change: Keep p0509's Stage 0/1 to get `best` at N=42496. Then: (1) active = cells with h>1e-12*h.max(), u0=log(h[active]); (2) define grad(u) as the exact log-parametrised gradient of val=-log(num)+2log(s)+log(maxL) (reuse _norm_eq_fun_grad, multiply by h[active]); (3) Hv = (grad(u+eps*v)-grad(u-eps*v))/(2*eps) with eps=1e-6/||v||_2; (4) 25-step Lanczos with full reorthogonalisation on H, report the 5 smallest Ritz values and lambda_min; (5) if lambda_min < -1e-9, for w = the corresponding Ritz vector and s in {0.02,0.05,0.1,0.2} (on ||du||_inf) take u0 +/- s*w/||w||_inf, rebuild h, _rescale_maxL, compute exact R_of, accept the best if it beats bestR, then run full+window polish to deadline; otherwise print lambda_min and spend the remaining time in p0509's alternating window/full polish loop. Print lambda_min and the accepted delta.
experiments.prediction: lambda_min within +/-1e-6 of 0 (degenerate plateau, no negative curvature) and no gain, i.e. the point is a genuine local max; if lambda_min < -1e-6 and any downhill move survives exact-R + repolish, the saturation is curvature-limited and follow-ups should ride that eigenvector.

experiments.hypothesis: The one analytically exact compact-support flat autoconvolution is f(t)=t^{-1/2} on [0,T], whose self-convolution is EXACTLY constant on [0,T] and then tapers on [T,2T]; superposing a second such block starting at T adds an increasing contribution over [T,2T] that cancels the first block's decreasing taper, in principle widening the effective plateau. All previous superposition work used copies of the incumbent or rectangles at geometric scales, never this exact-plateau generator with taper cancellation.
experiments.change: Add a seeding stage before p0503's optimisation. Block profile on a segment of width w at offset x0 with amplitude a: h(x)=a/sqrt(x-x0+delta) with delta=w/512, so each block has an exactly flat self-convolution over its own width. Build seeds on a 2048-cell grid: block 0 on [0, w0] and blocks 1..K-1 at offsets W_k (contiguous, W_{k+1}=W_k+w_k) with widths w_k = r^k*w0, K in {2,3}, w0 = 0.5*N*{0.6,0.8}, r in {0.5,0.7}, amplitudes a_0=1 and a_k in {0.5,1.0} (9-12 seeds). For each seed: mass-rescale, 250 exact L-BFGS iterations (p0503's _exact_lbfgs) at N=2048, record R_of. Take the best coarse candidate, then ladder it up by 2x (heights held constant, each fine cell = its parent, mass rescale) with 400 exact L-BFGS iterations + _window_polish at each rung up to 42496, accepting only exact-R improvements; then hand the best to p0503's alternating full/window polish loop until the deadline. Print each seed's coarse R and the final R.
experiments.prediction: Coarse R of the best block seed is 0.85-0.93, the ladder ends at exactly 0.940794 (+/-1e-7) after the polish absorbs it, i.e. the taper-cancellation mechanism is real but lands in the same basin; a final R strictly above 0.9407945 would identify the first genuinely different basin found in 80 generations.

experiments.hypothesis: The loss Sigma_j L_j(M-L_j)/M is concentrated where L ~ M/2, i.e. in the mid band of the taper, and every previous taper move was either deterministic (F491, F504) or single-cell/block-discrete (F398, F404, F475). Randomised joint perturbations of the cells that generate the mid band, each followed by a local re-optimisation and accepted only on exact R, has never been run; if the taper holds any slack this finds it, and if not it bounds the slack.
experiments.change: Keep p0509 Stages 0/1 to get `best`. Compute Lf=_knots(best), M=Lf.max(), band = indices j with 0.30*M <= Lf[j] <= 0.70*M. Relevance per cell: rel = convolve(band_indicator, best) (same convolution as L but with the 0/1 band vector), normalised by its max; free_pool = cells with rel > 0.05. Then loop until 0.5 s before the deadline: draw sigma uniformly from {0.02,0.05,0.10} and a random 30% subset S of free_pool; multiply best[S] by exp(N(0,sigma)) (np.random with a fixed seed), rescale max(L)=1; run _exact_lbfgs on the contiguous window [min(S), max(S)] (capped at 8000 cells) with maxiter=150, then compute exact R_of; if R > bestR+1e-12 accept, print 'restart k R=...', and every 20 accepted-or-not restarts run one full _full_polish and one _window_polish on the current best. Keep a counter of best accepted improvement over the whole loop and print it at the end.
experiments.prediction: Total improvement <= 1e-7 over 0.9407944 (the taper is already converged and no random joint move survives), with the accepted-delta histogram concentrated at 0; a gain > 1e-6 would prove the taper band has residual freedom that only joint randomised moves can reach.

plan.analysis: Since gen 83, 40+ probes (free-set, taper-split, resolution, superposition, cone-space, DE multistart, symmetric subspace) all land on exactly 0.9407944 (F495/F500/F511/F517/F529). There is a reason: R is scale-invariant, so the max(L) derivative is a pure gauge direction — every surrogate (log-max, top-K, stop-grad quotient, F501) spans the same R-gradient, and the incumbent is a true local optimum for a very wide move set. Further polishing of the same basin is futile. Bets: (1) change the search *metric*, not the objective (Sobolev/H1-preconditioned L-BFGS), which has never been tried on a notoriously jagged (max/mean 97) iterate; (2) a shifted power-law family scan; (3) symmetric trapezoid-L targets with a spectral realizability test, to see whether a non-power-law, symmetric shape can exist at all.

experiments.hypothesis: Every optimiser so far takes L-BFGS steps in the plain Euclidean metric on log h, but the incumbent is extremely jagged (max/mean 97), so the useful step is a smooth, large-scale change of the profile that Euclidean L-BFGS never proposes. Preconditioning the gradient with (I - beta*Laplacian)^{-1} (an H1/Sobolev metric) turns each step into a smooth redistribution of mass and can reach points the Euclidean iterate cannot, without changing the objective at all.
experiments.change: Keep p0509's pipeline, but add a new stage after Stage 1 (full polish) and before Stage 1b: a copy of _exact_lbfgs (call it _exact_lbfgs_sobolev) whose inner f(u) computes val,g exactly as now (_norm_eq_fun_grad, K=1) and then replaces the gradient g_active by y = solve(I + beta*D^T D, g_active), where D is the first-difference operator on the *contiguous* active index list (use scipy.linalg.solveh_banded with the tridiagonal matrix: diagonal 1+2*beta, off-diagonal -beta). If the active set is not contiguous, fall back to plain gradient (print a warning). Run a ladder beta in {0, 4, 16, 64, 256} cells^2, each with maxiter 400/maxfun 800, warm-starting from the previous result, and after each beta run a plain (beta=0) full polish; keep the iterate only if R_of strictly increases. Then continue with the base's Stage 1b and alternating full/window loop unchanged. Print 'sobolev beta=%g R=%.7f' per rung and 'sobolev accepted R=%.7f'.
experiments.prediction: All rungs converge to the same point: printed R stays 0.9407944 to 7 digits (+/- 2e-6), and the final result equals the start. A gain above 1e-5 would prove the plateau was a metric artifact of Euclidean L-BFGS and not a true local optimum.

The incumbent is strongly asymmetric (f*f max near 0.18 of support), so the correct target class is an ASYMMETRIC profile: a very short ramp, a long plateau, and a power-law decay with tunable exponent q. plan.analysis: The 0.940794 point has survived ~50 structurally distinct attacks (F383/F472/F484/F495/F500/F511/F517/F529): every smoothing surrogate, every upsampling/coarsening, every coarse multistart, cone/spectral/target-fitting route returns exactly it. So the incumbent is almost certainly a strong (possibly global) optimum, and further gains must come from operators that act on the *exact* nonsmooth R rather than a surrogate, or from a genuinely different discretization/rounding of the knot sequence. I bet small: one exact-coordinate attack on the true R (a new operator), one Toeplitz-PSD rounding multistart (a different cone and a different rounding than F507/F485), and one order-statistic (quantile) max surrogate, which has a different gradient support than LSE/top-K-mean.

experiments.hypothesis: The point was only ever polished by gradient/bundle-like surrogates of max(L); it may not be a coordinate-wise maximizer of the exact R. Because num is quadratic in a single height, changing h_j to x makes num(x)=num0+g_j x+W x^2 exactly with g = _backprop(dq,h) (one FFT for all j) and W a j-independent constant, while max_m L_m(x)=max_t(L_{j+t}+2x h_t) is an exact max of N affine functions. So an exact per-coordinate 1-D maximization of the true R is cheap and vectorizable, and it can cross argmax switches that a single-argmax gradient cannot.
experiments.change: Insert one stage after the base's first full polish, keeping everything else. Add `_exact_coord_sweeps(h, deadline)`: loop until deadline; (1) compute Lf,num,dq via _num_and_dq(h), S=h.sum(), gvec=_backprop(dq,h), W=4*sum(q(h_k,h_{k+1})) (q as in the scoring formula, over the same shifted alignment); (2) candidates t = indices of the 64 largest h values plus the current argmax offset; (3) for each t and each of 40 trial x values in [0, xmax] (xmax = min(3*h_j, ...) chosen so S(x)>0), vectorized over all j: Rj(x) = (num + gvec_j*x + W*x*x)/((S+x)**2 * (Lf[j+t+1] + 2*x*h[t])) with Lf index shifted by the +1 padding, take the max over t; (4) per-coordinate best x_j, apply in random blocks of 1024 cells, recompute exact R_of after each block and keep the block only if R strictly increases (else apply only the single best coordinate); (5) after each sweep run the base _full_polish and _window_polish, keep only exact-R gains; print the number of coordinates whose optimal x_j differs from h_j by >1e-3 h_j and the resulting R.
experiments.prediction: Either R rises by 1e-5..1e-4 (the incumbent is not coordinate-wise optimal for the exact nonsmooth R), or R stays exactly 0.940794 with every optimal x_j equal to h_j to ~1e-4, which would establish coordinate-wise stationarity of the true objective — a new mechanism-level fact.

experiments.hypothesis: Every cone/spectral construction so far used the circulant relaxation (rfft>=0) or least-squares fitting (F507, F485, F416). The exact feasibility condition for L=h*h with h>=0 of length M is that the M-by-M Toeplitz matrix T(L) (T_ij=L[M-1+i-j]) is PSD and its lower Cholesky factor's first column is a valid h. Rounding a target through Toeplitz-Cholesky explores a strictly different (and correctly constrained) set of knot profiles than circulant clipping, so multi-scale plateau+shoulder targets may land in a different basin.
experiments.change: Add ONE stage before Stage 0, at M=512. Form the MxM symmetric Toeplitz T from the central part, symmetrize, eigen-decompose, replace eigenvalues by max(lambda,0), rebuild T'=V diag(lambda+) V^T. Take the lower Cholesky factor C of T'+1e-12*I; candidate h0 = C[:,0] (and also h0 = C[:,0]+C[:,1] and the |h0| clip variant). Evaluate exact R_of(np.clip(h0,0,None)) at N=M, keep the top 3 distinct candidates, ladder each up by 2x linear interpolation with exact L-BFGS polish at 1024/4096/16384/42496 (accepting only exact-R gains), and take the best if it beats the start. Then run the base pipeline unchanged.
experiments.prediction: All Toeplitz-rounded multi-scale candidates score below 0.93 at M=512 and, after laddering and polishing, none exceeds 0.940794; final R exactly 0.940794, confirming the incumbent is not reachable-or-beatable by PSD-Toeplitz rounding of plateau/shoulder targets.

experiments.hypothesis: All max-surrogates divide by the argmax knot itself (log max) or by the mean of the top-K (top-K mean), so with 19.6% of knots within 0.1% of max the gradient is dominated by the single extreme knot or by a mean that tracks it. Dividing instead by the p-quantile knot (the rank-floor(p*n) largest L) puts the gradient on ONE cell at rank p, at a different location, which pushes the near-max *body* down while allowing the peak to stay slightly higher — a trade-off no previous surrogate encoded.

Print the R and the final p that helped.

plan.analysis: Fifty generations of attempts have left the 0.940794 point unchanged: 53 recorded failures against local moves, smooth-max surrogates, resolution ladders, taper-target inversion, global multistarts, and cone/spectral constructions. Two escape mechanisms were never actually completed: (a) exact 1-D maximization of the true nonsmooth R along large *dense multiscale* directions (only single-coordinate versions were run, and p0553 died on CPU), and (b) a curvature probe (F487/F518 died on budget). info.open_why: p0497 is the common ancestor of the current best lineage and F495/F383 are the most-cited findings explaining why the 0.940794 basin is stuck; F497 gives the analytic loss decomposition and F510/F551 show what escape attempts already failed, so I can pick genuinely new directions.

plan.analysis: 0.940794 has survived ~59 structurally different escape attempts (smooth/singular seeds, cone/spectral, DE/CMA multistart, mirror paths, adaptive meshes, target inversion, upsampling), always returning identical f*f stats — strong evidence it is a global optimum of this discretisation. Two mechanisms are genuinely untested. (i) An exact, kink-free reformulation that carries the max as a free variable with a log-barrier, so no surrogate bias pins the argmax knot. (ii) Envelope-modulated *binomial* (exactly-flat-autoconvolution) seeds — the only family whose L is exactly constant — with a sharpness exponent controlling the taper. I bet one small crack exists at the shoulders; otherwise the basin is confirmed global, and a cheap structured local transfer search tests that directly.

experiments.hypothesis: Every surrogate used so far (log-max, top-K mean, LSE, quantile, penalty) is biased at the 19.6% near-max band, which freezes the geometry. Carrying the max as an explicit variable t with a log-barrier on t-L_j>=0 gives a smooth, unbiased objective whose interior path can slide all near-max knots simultaneously.
experiments.change: Add a stage after Stage B in p0564. Define F(h,t) = -log(num) + 2*log(sum h) + log(t) - (1/mu)*sum_j log(t - L_j), optimised over (u=log h on active cells, w=log t) with scipy L-BFGS-B, gradients from the existing _num_and_dq/_backprop (barrier term adds (1/mu)*sum_j (1/(t-L_j))*dL_j/dh, and d/dw is -(1/mu)*sum_j t/(t-L_j) + 1). Start t = 1.02*max(L) and clip t-L_j to >=1e-12. Run a mu ladder 1e2,1e3,1e4,1e5,1e6,1e7, warm-starting each rung, ~500 iterations per rung; final rung mu=1e8 with 800 iterations. After each rung build h, _rescale_maxL, and keep it only if exact R_of improves. Fill all remaining time with the base's alternating window/full polish on the best point.
experiments.prediction: Final exact R is either exactly 0.940794 (+0.000000), confirming even an unbiased exact max formulation cannot move the basin, or slightly higher with a measurably wider near-max band (>19.62% of knots within 0.1% of max).

experiments.hypothesis: h_k = C(2k,k)/4^k has h*h EXACTLY constant (generating function (1-z)^-1/2, squared gives (1-z)^-1), so its plateau is exactly flat; only its taper costs. A sharp multiplicative envelope E(k/K) makes the taper shorter than uniform truncation or raised-cosine, which is precisely the residual loss mechanism (F528).
experiments.change: Add a Stage 0 to p0548. At N=8192 build seeds h_k = C(2k,k)/4^k * E(k/K) for k=0..K-1 (zeros after), with C(2k,k)/4^k computed by the stable recursion h_0=1, h_{k}=h_{k-1}*(2k-1)/(2k); envelopes E(x)=exp(-x^p) for p in {2,4,8,16} and E(x)=max(0,1-x)^q for q in {0.5,1,2,4}, and hard truncation; K in {0.25,0.40,0.55}*N. Rescale each to max(L)=1, polish each with 300 exact L-BFGS iterations, take the best 3 by exact R, 2x-upsample them (_rescale_maxL + linear interp) twice to N=42496 and run full exact L-BFGS polish on each; accept only strict exact-R gains over the start, then hand the best to the base's normal Stage A-C loop to spend the rest of the budget.
experiments.prediction: Raw seeds score ~0.90-0.93 and polished candidates land at or just below 0.940794; a gain would show the taper-corner sharpness, not plateau flatness, is the remaining lever. Report the best envelope/parameter.

experiments.hypothesis: If any headroom exists it is in the shoulder knot mass (F528): the incumbent's loss is concentrated where L~M/2. Build a list of directed transfer pairs (i,j): i over the ~150 cells with the largest |h_i|, j over cells whose generated knots straddle the shoulder band (0.05M < L < 0.6M, found by convolving the band indicator with h), plus any adjacent pair (i,i+1) inside the shoulder. If the best x gives strict R improvement, apply it, _rescale_maxL, run a 200-iteration full exact L-BFGS polish, keep if exact R still improves, and restart the sweep. Cycle sweeps until the deadline, keeping the best array; fall back to the base's window/full polish loop if a sweep yields nothing.
experiments.prediction: Cycles report gains of 0 or <1e-6, ending at 0.940794 (confirming the shoulders are exactly optimal), or a small genuine gain >1e-6 indicating residual shoulder mass was reachable.

plan.analysis: The 0.940794 point is saturated against ~60 structurally different levers, and the crucial structural fact is that R is exactly invariant to repeating each height k times: any uniform refinement is a score-neutral reparametrisation, so N was never the bottleneck and every upsample/refine bet was doomed by construction. What remains is (a) the shape-level global question and (b) exact second-order information, which has only been probed by a 25-step Lanczos run. I bet on: a full-Hessian Newton/saddle escape at reduced resolution where it is affordable; a cheap coarse-resolution multistart that deliberately tests a *different* basin; and neutral (tie-accepting) drift along the huge near-tie ridge, since all prior escapes demanded strict improvement.

experiments.hypothesis: The incumbent is a saddle or a very flat minimum of the smooth -log R objective, and L-BFGS's limited-memory metric cannot see the shallow negative directions that the 1024x1024 full Hessian can. At N=1024 a full Hessian costs 2048 cheap gradient evaluations, so genuine Newton steps and exact negative-curvature directions become affordable.
experiments.change: Add a new stage after the existing Stage 1. (1) Map the current best to N_r=1024 by mass-conserving cumulative resampling (reuse _resample_cum), then _rescale_maxL and run _exact_lbfgs to convergence. (2) With the argmax knot m frozen, build the exact Hessian of F(h)=-log(num)+2log(sum h)+log(L_m) in u=log h over the active coordinates by central differences (eps=1e-6) of the analytic gradient returned by _norm_eq_fun_grad (gradient times h_u chain rule). (3) np.linalg.eigh it. If lambda_min < -1e-6 take its eigenvector v, do an exact-R line search on h*exp(t*v) for t in +-{1e-4,1e-3,1e-2,3e-2,1e-1} (rescale max L each time, keep the best exact R), then re-polish. (4) Also take 5 damped-Newton steps d=-(H+mu I)^-1 g with mu tuned so ||d||_inf<=0.5 and backtracking on F. (5) Repeat 1-4 until 60% of the budget is gone, then resample the best N=1024 array up to N=42496 and run the existing alternating full/window polish with the rest of the budget; return the best exact R seen at any resolution.
experiments.prediction: lambda_min will be around 0 to -1e-3; the negative-curvature and Newton steps will move R by less than 1e-6 and the final score will be 0.940794 again, confirming the point is a genuine (near-)local max of the exact objective, not an L-BFGS artefact. A gain of >=1e-5 would mean the incumbent is a shallow saddle.

experiments.hypothesis: Because R is exactly repeat-invariant, the shape problem can be searched exhaustively at N=384 for a few seconds; if the coarse landscape has any basin other than the incumbent's that scores within ~1% of it, that basin is a genuinely unexplored starting shape for the 42496-cell polish, which is the only thing that has never been tried (all prior escapes perturb the incumbent).
experiments.change: Add a Stage 0 before the existing pipeline. Block-average the start to N=384 (mass-conserving) and record its coarse signature sig(h) = (argmax of L divided by 2N, fraction of L-knots above 0.95*max, fraction of cells with h > 0.1*mean). Then at N=384 run ~2500 random starts: each h = exp of a random piecewise-linear log-profile with 8 random knots in [0,384] and values uniform in [-3,3], clipped positive, then 300 L-BFGS iterations of _norm_eq_fun_grad; keep every result with R>0.90. Cluster them by signature, discard the cluster matching the incumbent's signature, and take the best remaining candidate. Resample it to N=42496 (_resample_cum, then _rescale_maxL) and spend ALL remaining budget on alternating _exact_lbfgs (K=1, 1500 iters) and _window_polish_shift; never replace the start's score unless strictly exceeded, and return the best of {start, this candidate}.
experiments.prediction: The coarse incumbent scores ~0.93-0.94 at N=384 and no distinct basin will exceed ~0.93 there; after full polish that alternative lands at or below 0.940794. Reporting the coarse score gap tells us how strongly one basin dominates the shape landscape.

experiments.hypothesis: 19.62% of f*f knots sit within 0.1% of the maximum and 42.8% within 5%, so there is a very large ridge of near-tied shapes; every previous escape rejected tie moves and could only move where the gradient was already non-zero. Accepting neutral moves lets the point diffuse along the ridge until it reaches a place with a usable descent direction.
experiments.change: Replace the escape/hopping part of the pipeline with a neutral-drift loop that spends the whole budget. Maintain cur (current point) and best. Each iteration: pick a random window of contiguous cells of length L in [8, N/16] (log-uniform), apply a smooth multiplicative perturbation inside the window (Gaussian-smoothed log-noise, sigma=L/8, amplitude drawn from a schedule decaying as 3e-2 * (remaining/30)^0.7), then run _exact_lbfgs on ONLY that window's cells with maxiter 30. If R(cur') >= R(cur) - 1e-10 accept cur=cur' (neutral moves allowed); if R(cur') > R(best)+1e-15 also set best=cur'. Every 200 iterations re-run a full _exact_lbfgs (K=1, 600 iters) from cur and accept under the same neutral rule. Return best (best is only ever updated on strict gains, so this is safe).

plan.analysis: The 0.9407944 point has survived ~70 structurally different attacks (families, cone/PSD relaxations, exact Hessians, neutral drift, resolution ladders, padding, superposition). info.open_why: See the current best pipeline's exact stages and the key findings about why the 0.940794 basin resists escape, so I can pick experiments that attack a genuinely different axis rather than repeat failed polish/upsample/perturbation variants.

plan.analysis: The 0.940794 point is extremely saturated: 97 generations of local, global, resolution, target-fitting, and surrogate attacks all return exactly the same R. The remaining loss is the taper: 1-R = sum L(M-L)/(M sum L), so the only way forward is a shape whose L is closer to a flat plateau with sharper edges. I am betting on two new levers: (1) reparameterising the taper knot values directly, via exact deconvolution, which searches the shape of L where the loss lives; (2) a low-dimensional generalized-beta random multistart to test a genuinely different basin; and (3) a p-norm homotopy on the max surrogate to see whether the non-smooth max is the binding trap.

experiments.hypothesis: The residual loss is entirely in the taper band of L. If we reparameterise the taper knots with a monotone cubic spline through a few control points, then invert L back to h exactly by the forward deconvolution recursion, the resulting shape can have a sharper, more optimal taper than the incumbent's.
experiments.change: After the existing Stage 1 full polish, compute Lf=[0,conv(h,h),0], M=max(Lf). Identify the taper band T={j: 0.005*M < Lf_j < 0.995*M}. If T is nonempty, fit the normalized values u=Lf[T]/M by a monotone cubic interpolant through K evenly spaced control points (K=6,8,10,12). Reconstruct a trial knot vector Tgt: Tgt_j = M on the complement of T (clipped to [0,1]) and Tgt_j = M * spline(u) on T. Enforce Tgt>=0, Tgt[0]=0, Tgt[-1]=0. Deconvolve Tgt by the forward recursion h_0=sqrt(Tgt_0), h_k=(Tgt_k - sum_{i=1}^{k-1} h_i h_{k-i})/(2 h_0) for k>=1 (guard h_0>1e-12). Clip negative h to 0, rescale max(L)=1, then run a short exact-LBFGS polish and accept only if exact R strictly improves over the incumbent. Try all K and keep the best.
experiments.prediction: If the taper is suboptimal, at least one K gives a strict gain (>=1e-6). If the incumbent's taper is already optimal, R stays exactly 0.9407944 and confirms the taper is saturated.

experiments.hypothesis: The incumbent may be a local optimum in the smooth-function class, but a flexible low-dimensional parametric family searched globally can find a different basin. A generalized-beta profile with a multiplicative sinusoid covers singular, plateau, and oscillatory shapes and has only 6 parameters, so random search is cheap and exhaustive.
experiments.change: At the start, before any polishing of the start, run a random multistart at N=2048 over h(x) ∝ x^a (1-x)^b * (1 + c sin(2π d x + e))^f with a,b ∈ [0,1.5], c ∈ [0,0.8], d ∈ [0.5,5], e ∈ [0,2π], f ∈ [0.5,3]. Draw 20000 samples with a fixed RNG, evaluate exact R at N=2048 via FFT (fast), keep the top 20 candidates by R, mass-upsample (cumulative-mass interpolation) each to N=42496, and run a short exact-LBFGS polish on each. Accept any candidate that beats the incumbent R; spend the remaining budget polishing the best.
experiments.prediction: If the incumbent is a global or near-global optimum within this family, no candidate beats 0.9407944. A gain >=1e-5 would reveal a new basin; a small gain confirms the family is too restrictive.

experiments.hypothesis: The non-smooth max term may be trapping the optimizer in a flat, pinned configuration. A p-norm homotopy (p increasing from 2 to 64) replaces max(L) by a smooth surrogate that initially weights all knots, then gradually concentrates on the maximum, potentially following a better descent path than the direct exact max.
experiments.change: After the initial full polish, replace the exact -log R objective by the smooth surrogate F_p(h) = -log(num) + 2 log(sum h) + (1/p) log(sum Lf^p), where Lf=[0,conv(h,h),0] and p is a ladder (2,4,8,16,32,64). For each p, run L-BFGS in log-h coordinates for a fixed number of iterations (e.g., 300) using the analytic gradient of F_p (backprop through conv). After the ladder, run the existing exact -log R polish and accept only if exact R improves. Keep the best exact-R construction throughout.
experiments.prediction: If the exact max term is the binding trap, the homotopy reaches a shape with R > 0.9407944 after exact polish. If the incumbent is a true local optimum of the exact objective, R stays at 0.9407944 and confirms the non-smooth max is not the bottleneck.

plan.analysis: The 0.940794 incumbent has now absorbed ~80 structurally different attacks (top-K, LSE, p-norm, cone, band-pinning, upsampling, kicks, multistarts) with literally zero gain, so further direct polishing bets there are near-worthless. The only live signal is F581/p0584: top-k peak smoothing plus shifted peak-window polishes moved an *unsaturated* basin (0.940639→0.940651). So I bet on porting that lever to the closest unsaturated basins (0.940787, 0.940651), which are different local optima where slack may remain, and spend one slot testing whether large-amplitude (not tiny) window kicks can leave the incumbent's basin at all.

experiments.hypothesis: The 0.940787 point is a distinct, less-saturated local optimum than 0.940794. Keep best only on strict exact R gain. Spend the whole budget; deadline = t0+budget-1.0.
experiments.prediction: Either exact R exceeds 0.940795 on some rung (new best, showing 0.940787's basin has slack and is not the incumbent's basin), or every rung collapses onto 0.9407944 (same attractor).

plan.analysis: The 0.940794 incumbent has survived ~100 structurally different attacks, and the neighbouring 0.940791/0.940789 basins have each been closed by dedicated runs (F596/F608/F610). So the realistic target is a micro-gain, and only two mechanisms have ever paid at this level: top-k peak smoothing (F581/F590/F607, worth 1e-5 on unsaturated basins) and zero-pattern changes (F265 floor/prune, +2e-5 once). info.open_why: The 0.940791/0.940789 basins (p0595/p0600) are less saturated than the incumbent and F581/F590/F607 show top-k ladders actually gain there, so I want their exact code and evidence to plan three experiments that exploit that live line.

plan.analysis: The 0.940794 point is saturated against local levers, argmax-freezing, smoothing surrogates, resolution escalation and every discrete repair; all remaining near-equal points have literally the same f*f statistics (0.967314/0.910043), and the only gains in 100 generations came from climbing weaker basins (0.940787->0.940791) via flattening surrogates. So I bet on three floor-safe attacks from p0579: (1) a band coefficient-of-variation flattener (variance, not mean, of near-max knots - a direction never tried); (2) signed relaxation of the non-negativity constraint, then projection and polish - a genuinely new basin generator; (3) selective sub-cell refinement of *only* the taper cells with the flat region frozen, since F578 locates all residual loss in the taper.

experiments.hypothesis: Every flattening surrogate so far rewarded raising the *mean* of the top-K knots (top-k mean, p-norm, LSE), which also raises max(L) and thus pays a log(M) penalty. Minimizing the dimensionless variance (coefficient of variation squared) of the near-max band flattens the plateau without rewarding a higher level, which is the actual Hoelder deficit: num/(s^2*M) is maximized by equal knots, not by high ones.
experiments.change: Keep p0579's helpers (_knots, R_of, _num_and_dq, _backprop, _rescale_maxL, _exact_lbfgs, _window_polish). deadline=t0+budget-2.5. Add _cv_obj_grad(h, lam): s=sum(h); num,dq,Lf=_num_and_dq(h); M=Lf.max(); band = indices with Lf>=0.99*M, truncated to the 4000 largest by Lf; m1=band mean, M2=band mean of (L-m1)^2, c2=M2/m1^2; obj=-log(num)+2*log(s)+log(M)+lam*c2; gLf=-dq/num; gLf[argmax]+=1/M; for j in band: gLf[j]+=lam*(2*(Lf[j]-m1)/K/m1^2 - 2*c2/m1/K); grad=_backprop(gLf,h)+2/s; return obj, grad[free]*h[free]. Add _cv_lbfgs(h0,lam,maxiter,deadline) mirroring _exact_lbfgs (u=log h on active cells, L-BFGS-B, ftol 1e-18, gtol 1e-15, TimeoutError callback). Main loop until process_time()>deadline-2.0, cycling lam in [0.05,0.2,1.0,0.5], each rung followed by _exact_lbfgs(cand,600) and _window_polish(cand, frac=0.25, extra=8, shift cycling 0,+1,-1,+2,-2); accept only if R_of(cand) > bestR. Finish with _exact_lbfgs(best,2500). Return best.
experiments.prediction: Either R exceeds 0.940794 (new best, +1e-6 or more, showing the plateau's variance and not its level was the binding defect), or every rung returns exactly 0.9407944 (the point is a joint local max in both level and variance).

experiments.hypothesis: R>1 is possible for signed f (Hoelder uses f>=0), and a signed f with a nearly flat autoconvolution exists (e.g. convolution square roots of Fejer-like kernels). The non-negativity constraint, not the flatness deficit, may be what pins us at 0.940794; projecting a high-R signed solution back onto the non-negative orthant is a basin generator no previous experiment has used (all prior work stayed inside the non-negative cone, log-parameterised).
experiments.change: Keep p0579's helpers. deadline=t0+budget-2.5. In LINEAR coordinates x (no log), define _signed_obj_grad(x): num,dq,Lf=_num_and_dq(x); s=x.sum(); if |s|<1e-9 return 1e18,zeros; gLf=-dq/num; gLf[argmax(Lf)]+=1/Lf.max(); obj=-log(num)+2*log(|s|)+log(Lf.max()); grad=_backprop(gLf,x)+2*sign(s)/|s|. Add _signed_lbfgs(x0,maxiter,deadline): minimize with method L-BFGS-B, bounds [(-2*A,2*A)] with A=4*max(start)+1e-12, ftol 1e-20, gtol 1e-16, TimeoutError callback; return res.x. Build signed seeds from start: x0=start; x0=start - roll(start, d) with d=index of the flat band width (computed from Lf>=0.99*M on the start); x0=2*start - roll(start,d) - roll(start,-d). For each seed, run _signed_lbfgs (iterations 2500), report num/(s^2*max) but never accept it as the answer; then form three projections xp in {clip(x,0,None), |x|, clip(x+0.5*max(0,-x.min()),0,None)}, rescale each with _rescale_maxL, then _exact_lbfgs(xp,2500) + _window_polish(frac=0.30,extra=8) + _exact_lbfgs(1500), and accept only if R_of exceeds bestR (initialised to R_of(start)). Loop over seeds/projections until deadline-1.0, then final _exact_lbfgs(best,2500). Return best.
experiments.prediction: The signed optimum will show R_signed well above 0.95 (much flatter autoconvolution), but all non-negative projections will polish back to <=0.940794. A projection that beats 0.940794 would prove the incumbent is only a constrained local optimum and would open a new class of constructions.

experiments.hypothesis: F578 localises essentially all of the residual loss in the taper band of L, and F609/F615 show moving mass on the coarse grid buys nothing. The taper is the one place where extra degrees of freedom have never been given *alone*: every escalation freed the flat region too, letting L-BFGS drift there and lose the gain. Refining only the taper cells (flat region frozen, mass conserved, so R is bit-identical before polishing) targets the loss directly and is monotone-safe.

Also try a second refinement round on the surviving taper cells only (again split free cells in two, mass conserved, N<=200000 guard). Return the best array (report its own N; do not contract).

plan.analysis: The 0.9407944 point has now absorbed ~110 structurally different attacks (F495/F500/F511): local (Newton, SQP, coordinate-1D, frozen argmax), surrogate (top-k, p-norm, LSE, CV, quantile), resolution (upsample, taper-split, repeat), and global (DE, CMA-ES, singular seeds, target inversion). Meanwhile nothing has tried a non-infinitesimal move in the g=h*h domain, or coherent *sharpening* (only smoothing/random kicks). I bet one refinement for a last 1e-7 and two genuinely different structural probes.

experiments.hypothesis: p0626's K-log is identical for K=30,15,8,4,2,1 (one short L-BFGS batch per rung), then it stalls in polish loops that F612 shows converge in <4 s. F590/F581/F607 show the productive unit is a *multi-cycle* small-K ladder with shift-cycled peak windows and periodic exact K=1 polishes; this recipe has never been run to completion on p0626's 0%-zero shape (its shape differs from both 0.940789 and 0.940651 where it worked).

experiments.hypothesis: All previous moves are local (gradients, windows, small/random kicks) or fresh absolute seeds. R depends only on the knot sequence L=g=h*h, and the residual loss is the deficit of the near-max band. A non-infinitesimal, mass-preserving map applied *in g-space* (g' = M*(g/M)^p, p<1 raises shoulder knots toward M while leaving small knots small) followed by exact deconvolution back to heights is a coherent global reshaping that no experiment has tried (F578/F537/F541 fitted external targets; F548 only did line searches along directions in h).

For p in [0.92,0.85,0.70]: g=convolve(hc,hc); Mx=g.max(); g2=Mx*(g/Mx)**p; g2*=g.sum()/g2.sum(); invert exactly by the positive square-root recursion (h2[0]=sqrt(g2[0]); for k=1..n-1: h2[k]=(g2[k]-2*dot(h2[1:k],h2[k-1:0:-1]))/(2*h2[0])), clip negatives at 0; rescale_maxL; then ladder up x2 (linear interp) with _exact_lbfgs(K=1,400,800,deadline) at 4096, 8192, 16384, 32768, 42496; then alternate _window_polish and _exact_lbfgs(K=1) on that candidate until its time slice or deadline; track the global best over all p and the original start by exact R.
experiments.prediction: The polished candidates land back at 0.9407944 or slightly below; a strict gain would show the shoulder knots (not the peak) were the binding constraint, and that g-space reshaping with exact inversion can leave this basin.

experiments.hypothesis: Every escape attempt used smoothing, blurring, or random multiplicative kicks (F466/F527/F551/F586), i.e. moves that lower max/mean. The incumbent's f*f peak sits at only 0.233 of support with max/mean 97, which is consistent with the optimum wanting sharper endpoint behaviour (the exact flat solutions are arcsine-singular: h_k~k^-1/2). experiments.change: budget split evenly over q in [1.10,1.25,1.50,2.00,0.70]. For each q: hq=clip(start,0,None); hq=(hq/hq.mean())**q; hq=_rescale_maxL(hq); then within its slice run _exact_lbfgs(hq,maxiter=800,maxfun=1600,deadline,K=1) then up to 6 alternating _window_polish(frac=0.25,extra=8) and _exact_lbfgs(K=1,400) passes, always keeping only strict exact-R improvements; finally, for the best candidate of the whole run, spend any remaining budget on repeated _full_polish + _window_polish to the deadline. Use time.process_time() checks with a 1.0 s margin.

info.open_why: p0626 is the incumbent; F495 is the most-cited 'stuck' finding; F581/F590/F607 are the only recent 'works' findings showing where gains still come from (weaker basins, top-k ladders), and F529 is the analytic flat-autoconvolution seed that might be a genuinely different starting point.

plan.analysis: The 0.940794 point has resisted ~100 generations of local, surrogate, resolution, and seed-family attacks. The remaining structural suspects are (i) the theoretically exact multi-block singular construction, which has never been globally searched over free block positions/amplitudes beyond K=2-3 geometric blocks; (ii) the possibility that the incumbent is a non-monotone local optimum even though the exact flat-autoconvolution generator is monotone decreasing; (iii) under-resolution of the sharp left-edge singularity by a uniform 42496-cell grid. I bet one of these three changes either finds a new basin or explains why the incumbent is saturated.

experiments.hypothesis: The exact flat-autoconvolution block h(x)=a/sqrt(x-x0+delta) has an exactly constant self-convolution on its own width; superposing several such blocks can cancel the first block's taper with later blocks' rising cross terms. F519 only tested K=2-3 blocks with geometric widths. A free global search over K=3-6 blocks with independently optimized positions and amplitudes may find a wider flat plateau that the incumbent's generic local polish cannot reach.
experiments.change: Add a stage before the existing polish loop. Build h on a coarse grid Nc=4096 as h(x)=sum_{k=1..K} a_k * (x-x_k+delta)^(-1/2) for x>x_k, 0 elsewhere, with x_1=0, delta=1e-8. Parameterize the K-1 gaps by a softmax: let s in R^{K-1}, g=softmax(s)*(1-eps), x_{k+1}=x_k+g_k, and a_k=exp(t_k) with t in R^K. Run scipy.optimize.differential_evolution on exact R_of at Nc=4096 for K=3,4,5,6, with maxiter=150, popsize=15, tol=1e-6, seed=0. Take the top 3 candidates per K, evaluate the same continuous h on N=42496, then for each run _exact_lbfgs (full, maxiter=1500) and _window_polish, accepting only if exact R > bestR. Print DE coarse R for each K and final polished R. Spend remaining budget in the existing alternating window/full polish loop.
experiments.prediction: DE coarse R will be 0.88-0.94. After polish, every candidate either lands exactly at 0.940794 (incumbent is in the closure of this family) or one candidate gives a strict gain, identifying multi-block singular taper cancellation as the missing mechanism.

experiments.hypothesis: The exact flat-autoconvolution generator f(x)=x^{-1/2} is monotone decreasing. The incumbent may be a non-monotone local optimum: unconstrained L-BFGS can oscillate heights, and those oscillations may waste loss. Constraining h to be nonincreasing (h_0 >= h_1 >= ... >= h_{N-1}) removes those degrees of freedom and may reveal a better monotone basin.
experiments.change: Add a monotone-constrained optimization stage after the start. Parameterize h_i = sum_{j=i}^{N-1} v_j with v_j = exp(z_j), so h is automatically nonincreasing and positive. Initialize v_j = max(h_j - h_{j+1}, 1e-12) (h_N=0) and z=log v. Compute the exact -log R value and gradient in h via _norm_eq_fun_grad, then transform to v by grad_v_j = sum_{i=0}^j grad_h_i (np.cumsum(grad_h)) and to z by grad_z = grad_v * v. Run scipy.optimize.minimize L-BFGS-B on z with bounds (-30,30), maxiter=3000, ftol=1e-20, gtol=1e-16, deadline-aware callback. Take the result h_mono, run _exact_lbfgs (full) and _window_polish on it, and accept only if exact R improves on bestR. Print R after monotone polish and after unconstrained polish. Then continue the existing loop.
experiments.prediction: The monotone-constrained optimum has R <= 0.940794. If it is strictly below, the incumbent is not monotone-optimal and the constraint is binding; if it matches 0.940794, monotonicity is not the missing lever and the incumbent is already monotone-optimal.

experiments.hypothesis: The residual loss lives in the taper band, and the exact generator x^{-1/2} is singular at the left edge. A uniform 42496-cell grid may under-resolve that singularity; linear upsampling cannot create more resolution near x=0. A power-law remeshing that clusters cells near the left edge (or right edge) should capture the singular behavior better and lower the loss.
experiments.change: Add a remeshing stage. For p in {1.3, 1.6, 2.0, 2.5, 3.0, 0.7, 0.5}, build h_p of length N=42496 by h_p[i] = h[ int(round( (i/(N-1))**p * (N-1) )) ] for i=0..N-1. This is a nonuniform resampling of the same step shape. For each p, run _exact_lbfgs(h_p, maxiter=1500, maxfun=3000, deadline) then _window_polish, and accept only if exact R > bestR. Print R before and after polish for each p. Then spend remaining time in the existing alternating window/full polish loop.
experiments.prediction: If the left-edge singularity is under-resolved, one of the p>1 remeshings gives a small gain (>1e-5) after full polish; otherwise every p returns exactly 0.940794, confirming the uniform 42496 grid is not resolution-limiting in the singular direction.
