plan.analysis: 858 findings confirm the 0.940795 basin is saturated against essentially every local, global, coarse, fine and knot-space lever; the only gains in 140 generations came from weaker basins that still had slack. I bet on three mechanisms not yet tried in this combination: (1) an exact dense Newton step on the active boundary-layer cells, testing whether the L-BFGS metric is the last bottleneck; (2) 4x sub-cell free-split resolution restricted to the rise/fall band, testing whether the boundary layer needs finer-than-2x structure; (3) an objective-driven adaptive mesh that merges/splits cells to concentrate resolution where the loss actually lives. All three use the whole budget and accept only strict exact-R gains.

experiments.hypothesis: The point is a local max of -log R in the 42496-dim space, but L-BFGS's limited-memory metric may still miss a shallow curved valley in the ~600 cells that control the rise/fall band (where 1-R lives). An exact dense Newton step on just those cells, using the true Hessian built from FFT Hessian-vector products, can follow curvature that L-BFGS cannot, and a backtracking line search on exact R makes it safe.
experiments.change: After loading and rescaling start, compute the analytic gradient g of -log R. Select the 600 cells with largest |g_i|. Build the exact 600x600 Hessian of -log R restricted to those cells by 600 central finite differences of the analytic gradient (step 1e-6*max(h)), each gradient evaluation using the existing FFT backprop. Add ridge 1e-8*trace/n. Solve H d = -g, clip h+d at 0, backtrack (alphas 1,0.5,0.25,...) on exact R_of, accept the first strict improvement. Repeat up to 6 times or until no gain. Then run the base's final full/window alternation loop to the deadline, keeping only strict gains.
experiments.prediction: Tie at 0.940795 if the point is a true local maximum; a gain of >=1e-7 would prove the L-BFGS metric, not the shape, was the remaining bottleneck.

experiments.hypothesis: 1-R is the L2 deficit of f*f from a rectangle and lies almost entirely in the rise and fall ramps. At N=42496 each ramp is resolved by only a few thousand cells, and every previous refinement (F622, F758) used 2x splits or only the outermost cells. A 4x mass-preserving split with free fractions over the whole rise/fall band (excluding the flat plateau where L>0.999M) gives the boundary layer genuine sub-cell freedom for the first time.
experiments.change: Prolongate best to N2=169984 by splitting each cell into 4 equal sub-cells. Parametrise the 3 internal split boundaries of each 4-group as log-fractions; free only the groups whose f*f knots lie in 0.0005M < L < 0.9995M (freeze plateau groups at equal splits, i.e. 1/4,1/2,3/4). Run L-BFGS-B on the free log-fractions with analytic gradient (chain rule through the split map then the existing convolution backprop), maxiter 4000, deadline-checked. Then run one full log-L-BFGS at N2. Accept the N2 result only if its exact R exceeds the rescaled incumbent's R; otherwise return to N=42496 and run the base's final full/window loop to the deadline.
experiments.prediction: Tie at 0.940795 if the boundary layer is already optimally resolved at native N; a gain >=1e-6 would show the ramps need finer-than-2x sub-cell structure.

experiments.hypothesis: Every refinement so far used a uniform mesh chosen in advance. The loss is highly non-uniform (concentrated where L crosses M/2), so an objective-driven adaptive mesh that repeatedly splits the cell adjacent to the largest local loss and merges the cell whose removal costs least should reach a better R at a different N than any fixed-N polish, because it spends resolution exactly where 1-R is generated.
experiments.change: Start from best at N=42496. Loop until deadline: compute L and per-knot loss w_j = L_j(M-L_j). Build ~40 split candidates (split the cell adjacent to the 40 largest w_j into two equal halves, mass-conserving) and ~40 merge candidates (merge the cell adjacent to the 40 smallest w_j with its smaller neighbour, mass-conserving). Evaluate exact R for each candidate (one convolution each), accept the single best strictly-improving move; if none improves, run a short log-L-BFGS polish at current N (maxiter 300) and continue. Keep 2000 <= N <= 200000. Every 100 accepted moves run a 40%-peak window polish. Return the best array seen.
experiments.prediction: The mesh drifts toward the rise/fall band; if uniform resolution was binding, a gain of 1e-6 or more appears; otherwise every move ties and the result stays at 0.940795.
